children.text: Four islands floating in the Camotes Sea between mainland Cebu and Leyte, where the guitar-shaped Lake Danao, clear cave pools, and the white sand of Santiago Bay all come together. Large resorts are scarce, making it a good place to experience unassuming island life.

The Camotes Islands are a cluster of islands in the Camotes Sea between mainland Cebu and Leyte to its east. They consist of Pacijan, Poro, Ponson, and the small island of Tulang; travelers mainly visit Pacijan Island (San Francisco) and Poro Island (Poro and Tudela), which are connected to each other by a causeway. Ponson Island forms its own municipality, Pilar, and being farther away, sees fewer visitors.
The islands have long carried the nickname "Lost Horizon of the South." Just
2 hours

by boat from Cebu City, yet with almost no large-scale development, they retain quiet roads winding through coconut groves, unassuming fishing villages, limestone caves, and clear lakes. A common story traces the islands' name to "camote," the Spanish word for sweet potato.
The islands cover a total area of about 236 km² and had a population of about 109,278 at the

census. They are divided into four municipalities: San Francisco on Pacijan Island, Poro and Tudela on Poro Island, and Pilar on Ponson Island. The highest point is Mount Altavista on Poro Island, at only
, so the terrain is mostly gentle limestone hills and flatland, and the mangrove forests on three of the islands were designated a protected area in
. The islands are also among those recorded when Magellan's expedition reached the Philippines in
April 1521
, and in a cave on Tulang Island a University of Michigan expedition from the United States excavated about 60 skeletons along with pottery and shell bracelets in
, showing that people have lived here for a very long time. On Poro, an endangered language called Porohanon is still spoken, ranked among the most endangered languages in the Visayas.

In the middle of Pacijan Island is Lake Danao, which looks like a guitar from above, and along the coasts of the two islands are scattered the wide white sand of Santiago Bay and resorts such as Mangodlong Rock (Pacijan Island) and Buho Rock (Poro Island), where you jump into the sea from cliffs. The limestone terrain across the islands holds several cave pools filled with groundwater, and slipping into the cool water to escape the midday heat is a big part of the fun of a Camotes trip.

This is a place better suited to those who prefer renting a motorbike and unhurriedly touring beaches and caves one by one than to anyone seeking flashy nightlife or big resorts — independent travelers, and Korean families living in the Philippines looking for a weekend escape close to Cebu.

A freshwater lake in San Francisco, in the north of Pacijan Island, said to cover about 650 hectares (around 700 hectares according to some sources) and shaped like a guitar when seen from above. At Lake Danao Park on the shore, an entrance fee of about
lets you rent pedal boats, kayaks, and rafts, and 30 minutes of use costs about
. The course around the small island in the middle of the lake is popular; entrance fees differ from source to source, so it's safest to check on site.
A broad, curving stretch of white sand on the south side of Pacijan Island, considered the most photogenic beach in Camotes. The water is clear and the waves gentle, making it good for family swims.
Timubo Cave in San Francisco has a staircase leading down to a clear underground pool beneath stalactites. The entrance fee is low, and the cool water makes it a good midday stop.
Bukilat Cave in Tudela, Poro Island, is a large cave where sunlight pours in through an opening in the ceiling, making for striking beams-of-light photos.
At cliffside resorts such as Mangodlong Rock and Buho Rock, you can jump from a few meters up into the clear sea. Non-guests can also enter for an admission or usage fee.

blocks.title: Mangrove causeway and touring the islands

children.text: A motorbike loop around both islands, passing mangrove forests near the causeway that links Pacijan and Poro, takes only half a day. Hills on the Poro Island side offer views of the sea toward Leyte.
Tulang Diyot Island, reached by small boat from the village of Tulang Daku at the northern tip of San Francisco, is a small island with white sand and clear water.
Paraiso Cave, close to Consuelo Port, has a turquoise underground pool inside a landscaped garden, with an entrance fee of about
. The water looks shallow but is deep, reaching chest height at high tide, so don't push yourself if you're a weak swimmer. Heaven Cave is a lesser-known swimming cave at about
, with a stretch where you have to duck low to pass when the water is shallow at low tide.

Boats from Poro Port back to Liloan leave in the afternoon, but the times differ from source to source, so if you plan to return from Poro to Liloan, check with the shipping company before you leave.
About
1 hour 20 minutes
from Manila to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB). Camotes has no scheduled air service, so you go via Cebu and then by boat.
A bus or van to Danao from the North Bus Terminal next to SM City Cebu takes about
1–1.5 hours
, with a fare of about

The most common route is the Jomalia Shipping RoRo from Danao Port to Consuelo Port on Pacijan Island. It sails about four times a day (roughly
), takes about
2 hours
, and costs about
(this includes a 20% fuel surcharge added since March
, which may be dropped when fuel prices stabilize). Departure times change often, so it's safest to check the shipping company's notices or an online booking site the day before you leave.
If you're staying around Poro or Tudela, the Super Shuttle Ferry from Pier 88 in Liloan, north of Cebu, to Poro Port is convenient. It sails at about
and
, takes about
2 hours 30 minutes
, and costs about
(fuel surcharge included). From central Cebu to Liloan Port is about
40 minutes–1 hour
by car. The Jomalia route that used to run from Mactan Island to Consuelo has been suspended as of
September 2026
Arrive at the port at least
1 hour

before departure and bring photo ID. On weekends and holidays boats fill up early, so it's safer to buy tickets in advance at the counter or on an online booking site, and ID is required to get the senior, disabled, or child discount.
From central Cebu it's about
30km
along the northern coastal road to Danao Port, about
1–1.5 hours

by car. The RoRo ferries at Danao and Liloan ports also carry cars and motorbikes, but fares differ by vehicle type and spaces fill up quickly on weekends and holiday periods. Unless your itinerary on the islands truly needs a car, leaving the car in Cebu and renting a motorbike on the island is cheaper and easier.
When you get off at Consuelo Port, habal-habal (motorbike taxi) and tricycle drivers are waiting. A ride to your accommodation costs about
, and chartering one for a day island tour is about
. If you drive yourself, renting a motorbike at about
a day gives you the most freedom.
Pacijan and Poro are linked by a causeway (a bridge through the mangroves) about
1.5km
long, so it's easy to ride back and forth by motorbike. Tulang Diyot Island is a
5–10 minutes
boat ride from Tulang Daku beach, and a round-trip boat fare plus environmental fee comes to about
. Jeepneys and vans also run, but their schedules are irregular, which makes them hard to plan around.
In the past there were fast craft to Camotes from Mactan Island or Pier 1 in Cebu City, taking about
1 hour 10 minutes–1 hour 30 minutes

, but as of 2026 guide sites say the fast craft from Mactan is not available. Before booking, check the shipping company's notices to see whether it is running, and if not, use the RoRo from Danao or Liloan.

Coming in from the Leyte side, there are said to be small passenger boats linking Ormoc Port with Hagutapay Port in Tudela and Pilar Port in the Camotes. However, the boats are old and the schedules are irregular and change often, so check the latest times at Ormoc Port or locally before you set out.
The dry season,
December–May
, is best overall, and within it,
March–May
— with calm seas and clear skies — is ideal for beaches and cliff diving. During
December–February
, the northeast monsoon can make the Danao–Consuelo crossing rough, so bring seasickness medication.
June–November
is the rainy season, with frequent afternoon showers, and cave pools can turn cloudy after heavy rain. From
August to November
, typhoons can cancel the RoRo ferry on some days, so it's a good idea to build a spare day into your schedule during this period.
During Holy Week, the
May
holidays, and the Christmas break, ferries get crowded with local Cebu travelers. Visit on a weekday and you can have the beaches and caves almost to yourself.
The average temperature on the islands is around

, and annual rainfall is about 1,600mm in San Francisco. Caves and beaches are deep enough for swimming at high tide, while some spots have the bottom exposed at low tide, so plan your timing around the tides. As for festivals, Tudela holds a Cassava Festival around the
December 8
feast of the Immaculate Conception, and Poro celebrates the feast of the Santo Niño on the third Friday of
January
. Accommodations and boats get crowded then, so book early.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
Most accommodations cluster around Santiago Bay on Pacijan Island and the coast of San Francisco. Mid-range beachfront resorts run about
a night, and village guesthouses are around

. Poro Island has a few clifftop resorts, good for a quiet sea view, but with fewer restaurants and amenities. High-end resorts are rare across the islands and facilities tend to be modest, so set your expectations accordingly.
Food centers on unassuming local dishes. Carinderias (local eateries) around the port and market serve grilled fish caught that day, kinilaw (fish cured in vinegar), and adobo for about

. Resort restaurants also serve seafood dishes alongside simple Western food, and many places do a beach barbecue in the evening. As the islands' name suggests, sweet potato and cassava snacks are common too, so try some at the market.
Think of accommodation as two bases. At Santiago Bay there's Santiago Bay Garden & Resort, right on the beach, with rooms for roughly
, and on the coast near Consuelo Port there's Mangodlong Paradise Beach Resort, with rooms from

and up, regarded as the islands' signature resort for its clifftop pool and views. Both have long been listed in many guides and booking sites, but rates and operating status change often, so check recent reviews. Budget stays include guesthouses and hostels in the
range.

On Santiago Bay beach is Pito's Sutokil, well known for sutokil. Sutokil, from Cebuano words, serves three cooking methods at one meal — grilled (sugba), soup (tuwa), and vinegar-cured raw fish (kilaw) — so you can sample seafood in many styles, at about

per plate. At the Agora Market in San Francisco town you can eat barbecue and local food cheaply, and just as the islands' name comes from sweet potato (camote), camote cue (fried sweet potato) and sweet potato sweets are popular as snacks and gifts.
The islands have only a handful of ATMs that frequently run out of cash. It's best to withdraw all the cash you'll need in Cebu or Danao.
Some stretches have few gas stations for motorbike rentals, so use the bottled gasoline sold at village shops and keep your tank well topped up.
Most island roads are paved, but access roads to caves and beaches can be unpaved or steep. If you're a beginner rider, it's safer to go with a habal-habal driver.
Cave pools have slippery floors and cold water, so bring aqua shoes and a light waterproof bag.
Ferries often don't have assigned seating, so the earlier you board, the better your seat. The first morning boat can sell out early.
Phone signal generally reaches villages and beaches but drops out inside caves and on remote coastlines.
Good photo spots are the curving shoreline of Santiago Bay, the light beams in Bukilat Cave, and the morning mist over Lake Danao.
Admission fees vary by site: roughly
for Bukilat Cave,
for Timubo Cave (plus an environmental fee of
for Paraiso Cave, and
for Buho Rock and Mangodlong Rock. Mangodlong Rock sometimes waives the admission fee if you have a meal, so ask on site.
Caves and beaches are deep enough for good swimming only at high tide. Ask your accommodation or a local driver for that day's tide times and plan your route around them.
On weekends and holidays boats and accommodations fill up early, so book ahead, and get to the port no later than
1 hour
before departure.
Always confirm the depth and tide conditions with on-site staff before cliff diving. Rocks are exposed and very dangerous at low tide.
Cave interiors have weak lighting and steep stairs. Children and elderly visitors should hold the railing and move slowly.
Avoid traveling by small boat in bad sea weather. The RoRo ferry can also be cancelled, so check notices.
There are almost no streetlights at night, making motorbike riding dangerous. Avoid long-distance riding after dark.
Using soap or shampoo, and littering, are banned at natural attractions such as the lake and caves.
During Typhoon Tino (Kalmaegi) in
November 2025

, Typhoon Signal No. 4 was raised over the Camotes Islands and northeastern Cebu, including Danao, suffered heavy damage. Some resorts and attractions may still be under repair or may have changed how they operate, so check whether they are open before you visit.

Cave pools may look shallow, but some reach chest height at high tide, and the narrow entrances make it easy to bump your head. If you have a respiratory or heart condition, avoid damp, cramped caves.
After a typhoon or power outage, electricity and tap water can be cut off in parts of the islands, so bring a power bank and drinking water.

40 minutes

About
1 hour
by ferry from Hagnaya Port in northwest Cebu, an island with quiet white sand beaches and great seafood.
About

by fast craft from Cebu to Tagbilaran, Bohol, then about

About

by fast craft from Cebu to Bohol, a resort destination famous for Alona Beach and hopping tours.
About
1–1.5 hours
by bus from central Cebu to Danao Port, it's the starting and return base for a Camotes trip and is also good for combining city sightseeing and shopping.
